utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yesterday, the Milan Lukic Defence filed their fifth motion for the admission of documents from the bar table requesting the admission of three death certificates into evidence. I am to ask the Prosecution whether they have any submissions to make on this motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. The Prosecution would like to respond to that motion that was filed yesterday. The documents in issue were disclosed to the Defence on the 5th of September, 2008, prior to the testimonies of any of the Varda witnesses and prior to the testimony from Prosecution experts who gave evidence in relation to the fates of the victims. The application is untimely, and the Defence had numerous opportunities to present this evidence previously and elected not to, and all matters related to the proof of death of victims has been exhaustively and finally litigated in this case. The information contained in these death certificates is already in evidence within Prosecution Exhibit 119 on page 1. The Defence presents these documents as if they are new; they are not. They are part of a body of data Ms. Tabeau has considered and has included already in her report. Beginning on page transcript -- page 6119 of the transcript, Mr. Alarid questioned Dr. Tabeau for over five pages of testimony as to the manner in which death certificates are applied for by family members and issued by governmental authorities. The information in these death certificates, including the believed date of death, is provided by the family member who may or may not have been a witness to the crime. Dr. Tabeau explained how she considered this information along with all other available information before preparing Prosecution Exhibit 119 and her subsequent clarification. The key information from these certificates has already been admitted into evidence and fully explored during the course of Dr. Tabeau's two appearances before this Chamber. In light of this, the Prosecution takes no position and defers to the Chamber. If the Chamber determines these documents will assist it in its work, the Prosecution does not oppose their admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think they should simply come in for completeness of the records. I agree that they are somewhat referenced in P119, but I don't think they're cumulative because they are the official government document, and considering the fact that I received them in September, they were untranslated, and so sometimes things get missed in a case with voluminous paperwork, especially untranslated. I think it's appropriate they come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I have a question for Mr. Alarid. Do they concern persons mentioned in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. All three are members of the Varda allegation, the seven alleged dead people of Varda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber will admit the documents. Now, Mr. Alarid, yesterday you indicated that the accused Milan Lukic desired to make a statement. How long will that statement be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Fifteen to 20 minutes. Fifteen, I would say, other than him speaking slow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are disposed to allow it with that time-limit in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So Mr. Lukic, you may make your statement of 15 to 20 minutes now. THE ACCUSED MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you. Statement of the Accused Milan Lukic: THE ACCUSED MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by listening to the Prosecution witnesses in this courtroom, I was on the verge of a nervous breakdown.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please come closer to the microphone, and read slowly. The interpreters do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are being asked to come closer to the microphone. In fact, you may sit. You may sit. You don't have to stand. Sit, and read a little slower. THE ACCUSED MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, listening in this courtroom to the Prosecution witnesses, frankly speaking, I was on the verge of a nervous breakdown. The nebulous things and lies that they said about me are completely unreasonable, especially given that they clearly indicate what the Prosecution is capable of doing. Throughout the Prosecution case, I had to take tranquilisers and painkillers because I could not stand the monstrous fabrications and lies similar to scenarios in horror movies. In order for you not to have a distorted picture of me, I decided to say a few words to you in order to tell you the truth about who I am and how I found myself in the war in 1992 in Visegrad. My purpose is to destroy the plan of the Prosecution. I was born in a mixed Muslim Serbian village Rujiste, a small village. I was born in an ethnically mixed small village of Rujiste where Muslims and Serbs lived. This village is on the right bank of Drina, some ten or so kilometres from Visegrad. I'm the youngest child of my parents. I was brought up and I grew up with my sister, two brothers, and my friends; Serbs and Muslims. We lived modestly, just like all other residents of the village. We were raised in a patriarchal atmosphere where honour and dignity were considered prime values. My father was orphaned in World War II because fascists during the war broke into the house and took his father away. Thanks to the good people and neighbours, both Serbs and Muslims, my father, his sister and brother, and their mother -- single mother survived all the horrors of World War II. My father, the long-suffered father, and my mother always taught us children that we should always help everybody in need regardless of their faith and ethnic background because one measures a man based on his characteristics and his integrity. This is why without any bias I had a lot of friends among Muslims. I played with them and shared whatever I had, frequently shared a meal or a bed in my home or in their home under watchful eye of our parents. Socialising with Muslims continued throughout elementary schooling, secondary schooling, and later on when I attended school in Belgrade and when I started working in Germany and in Switzerland. My first love was a Muslim girl. I always considered and still do Muslims -- I always think all the best about Muslims, just like I do about all other peoples. In Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the former Yugoslavia, people disregarded the faith of people they socialised with and their ethnic background. It was a beautiful country, and people lived in harmony. To this day, I maintain contact with many Muslims, nowadays unfortunately only by phone. The nationalists of the former Yugoslavia together with various mentors created hatred and disagreement in our country and destroyed a wonderful country. Following my mandatory military service lasting one year in Slovenia, I found myself in Belgrade where I attended university. I had various jobs as a student, and then in mid-1988 a school friend of mine from elementary school asked me to come and be a guest in the house of him and his parents. When I arrived in Germany, I soon understood that this was a paradise. I liked the country so much that I wanted to remain there. Since I was athletically talented, I obtained papers, residence papers and a job through a football club. I didn't mind doing various jobs as long as they were honourable. I remained in Germany for more than a year. I met a girl from Switzerland, and then I moved to Zurich. I started working and training football there. When the war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I was in Switzerland. In May of 1992, I came to visit my parents, and to my misfortune I was immediately mobilised by the public security station in Visegrad. I was assigned as reserve policeman in the public security station in Visegrad. I remained in that position three months, and later on I was assigned to a reconnaissance unit of the Army of Republika Srpska. Throughout the war, I had no command responsibility or position, nor did I engage in politics. I could not stand injustice, and I publicly spoke out against Mafia attitude, communist links that prevailed in Visegrad, and all those protagonists took their revenge against me. They killed my brother in his house in the presence of his wife, and nobody was ever brought to justice for that crime. I was young, innocent, and I had no idea what would come about and how war profiteers, communists, and various criminals would use everything they had to accuse me. Throughout the difficult days of war, as much as I could, I helped everybody of Muslim faith and origin. Even though I was not charged with rape, the Prosecution brought various women here to lie about this, about this alleged rape. I have always held women in great respect, and this is something that was instilled in me by my mother and my older sister. I could never stand rapists and those who used power, and they knew about that, and they never dared come close to me. Throughout the war in Visegrad, I had a girlfriend who was a well known doctor in the medical centre in Visegrad, and she was a well respected woman, and it is clear to everybody that all these stories about rape are just a fabrication of a sick mind. I only recognise love and respect, and I have nothing but despise for rapists. Currently I have two young girls and I always, as I said, held women in great esteem. Now that my girls need me the most, I unfortunately am not next to them. They suffer due to my absence, and they suffer even more due to these fabricated false accusations against me. I haven't seen my parents since 1998. You are well aware that in 1992, there were some 20 passengers Muslims that were kidnapped from a passenger train in Strpce. Those people disappeared without a trace. It is believed that all of them were liquidated. I was accused as the main perpetrator even though when the kidnapping took place, I was far away from the place of the incident. This is why the police of Serbia arrested me, and I spent 14 months in prison in Serbia. Throughout my stay in prison, I was subjected to various methods, including lie detectors, and after everything the court in Serbia acquitted me because there was no evidence confirming my guilt. I was even paid damages due to my unjustified stay in prison. As a result of that, I once again went abroad to work, and it was there that I found out that criminal proceedings were put in place against me due to alleged kidnapping of Muslims who were travelling on a bus in Severin in 1992. I had nothing to do with this incident either. Until a man from Serbia working for the state security stated in this court that he had information that the kidnapped Muslims were later seen in the public security station in Visegrad after the kidnapping, it is well known that at the time when these men were kidnapped, I no longer worked for the public security station in Visegrad. I was a soldier for the Army of Republika Srpska. Whoever organised this kidnapping and took these innocent people to the police station in Visegrad knows where these people ended up. People who are in charge of life and death in Visegrad -- who were in charge between 1992 and 1996, Perisic and Savovic knew much more about this. They can answer your questions as to why these people were kidnapped and where these innocent kidnapped people ended their lives. The Prosecutor here accused me of murders in Visegrad in private homes and in Bikavac. They accused me of crimes that I took no part in it. The Prosecution put on the list of victims many people who are died or who died before the war, and they also put the names of people who never even existed. As for the incident on the Drina River, I did not take part in it. One of the alleged survivors described a perpetrator who does not resemble me at all. The testimony of other two witnesses, one of them was a protected witness, MLD-025, and they made me as one of the co-perpetrators, and it has been proven that at the time of the crime they could not have been present at the site. You were able to see that this protected witness lied in order to protect himself. More than 90 percent of OTP witnesses linked me to this red Passat car as though it was some identifying mark, and this car in fact belonged to the police station in Visegrad. It is true that the red Passat was used by the members of the public security station in Visegrad. How this car came to be in possession of the public security station in Visegrad is something that Risto Perisic could tell you about. He is the chief of the public security station in Visegrad who was in that position between 1992 and 1996. When it comes to incident concerning the Zukic family, I can tell you this, that Bakira Hasecic from the women's association together with secret Bosnian services AID and SIPA pressured women, Zukic Dzenita and her sister, to come to The Hague Tribunal to falsely accuse me of taking a car away from their family and killing their family members, father, mother, and brother. Since these girls knew the truth, they knew that I had nothing to do with their car or with their family. They did not wish to come here to lie and accuse an innocent man, all the more so since they are pious women and they are afraid of God. The Zukic girls wanted to testify for my defence, but due to threats and the fact that their children's lives were threatened in Sarajevo, I gave up from calling them to come here to testify because it my duty to protect these honest and honourable girls, now women and mothers. They do have the right to know what happened to their father, mother, and brother, but not the way the Prosecution wants them. I would now like to address the issue of the Koran book that was seen here in the courtroom at my table. I was given this book as a gift by Muslim general whom I came to know here at the Detention Unit. He told me, Since you are an honest and pious man, I will give you this book to take it to the courtroom with you, to hold it in front of you so that any false witnesses and anybody who uses lies will be persecuted by devil. Whoever took this book to the courtroom was given minimal sentences, and why doesn't an honest and honourable Serb have the same fate? I read Koran several times, and had everybody who was involved in the war read Koran and Bible, there would have been no war. Your Honours, it was my desire to study Arabic language. I know a lot about Muslim faith, but I didn't convert into Islam even though I had a lot of respect for that religion. Your Honours, you are able to see that I'm innocent. It is up to you to be guided by professional and legal principles and norms. Please do not allow somebody else such as a media campaign to take charge of your conscience. The true perpetrators should be found and punished but not an innocent man. Do not allow this court to be used as a tool to achieve injustice. Do not give up in the face of these pressures. You need to set free an innocent man who has been falsely accused in public. I feel sorry for every single victim who fell in the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina and in Visegrad. The scum became rich, and innocent people fell victims. The life of me personally and my family since 1992 has been hell. I despise the war because that is the greatest enemy of an honest lie [as interpreted], and I would advise every man to flee any war-like situation. Having faith in your professionalism, I calmly await the judgement, and I thank you very much for allowing me to give this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Now, Mr. Cepic, for your closing remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Defence for Sredoje Lukic Closing Statement:

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Esteemed president of the Chamber, esteemed members of the Chamber -- [French on English channel] -- it is my pleasure to present our closing argument. First of all, we completely agree with Mr. Groome's assertion when he said that this case is not only about identification but also about inconsistencies. But we completely disagree that these inconsistencies are minor. Bearing in mind the magnitude of these inconsistencies, the explanation provided by the Prosecution is neither sufficient nor convincing. Contrary to the Prosecution's assertion that the Defence has presented this case in an artificial and unnatural manner, the closing argument of the Defence clearly indicates that the Defence has analysed and presented all the evidence in a full context. I would like to address the propositions put forward in the Prosecution's final brief and closing argument. I submit that they are based solely on assumptions rather than facts, and it is well known that all assumptions crumble in the face of a single fact. A distinguished and considerably more colleague who appeared before his court and who is now a judge in the UK has given me the following advice: Always check the references and footnotes contained in the Prosecution's submissions. In this particular case, we were astonished, not only I, but all members of our team to find a substantial lack of references, a large number of misquotes, and incorrect references leading to wrong conclusions. I will devote only one part of my closing argument to these incorrect references and misinterpretation of evidence. Let me start with witness VG-013. In paragraph 216 of the Prosecution final brief states that VG-013 has seen Sredoje Lukic on the occasion in question by making reference to transcript page 1031. We can see this part of the transcript in front of us which clearly indicates that she hasn't seen Sredoje Lukic on that occasion. What I would like to say about this witness, her testimony under oath in response to the questions, including the question asked by the esteemed president whether she has seen Sredoje Lukic, she clearly answered that she hasn't. She confirmed the same that in -- in -- that she didn't -- she didn't see Sredoje Lukic and that she didn't know him from before. Furthermore, she clearly stated that on that particular day she didn't see Sredoje Lukic. The Prosecution wanted to defy or to deny the authenticity of the interview of this witness by saying that the adages probably have edited part of this. It is simply illogical to me that this witness persistently quotes two names of perpetrators, and that is simply impossible for an editor to cut out the third name. The witness confirmed the authenticity of this interview page 1130, and the Prosecution had an opportunity in redirect to ask the question about the interview, which he failed to say. Furthermore, I would like to make reference to the testimony in the Vasiljevic case during which this witness never mentioned the involvement of Sredoje Lukic. I would particularly like to stress Prosecution Exhibit P62, which is a statement given by VG-013, given under no oath to the district public Prosecutor in Sarajevo in which it gave a full description of the incident without ever mentioning the involvement of Sredoje Lukic. In paragraph 167, the Prosecution designated Edhem Kurspahic as an alleged recognition witness. VG-013 stated that she had allegedly heard from Edhem Kurspahic that Sredoje Lukic was outside the house. However, there is not a single statement or interview given by Mr. Edhem Kurspahic with relation to this incident, which would enable us to verify whether Edhem really knew Sredoje Lukic. Asked about this issue, VG-013 was unable to give a reliable answer but only a supposition. That's referenced in the transcript, page 1121. At that time our team thought that there was a clear doubt about this question. However, we decided to take a step further in order to clarify the issue of whether Edhem Kurspahic really knew Sredoje Lukic. During yesterday's closing argument, the Prosecution wanted to downplay the fundamental importance of testimony of VG-018 related to Edhem Kurspahic, namely, after the incident VG-018 and her son VG-084 lived as refugees in Srebrenica together with Edhem Kurspahic; reference, transcript page 1360. It is only reasonable to conclude that they often discussed the Pionirska incident in the period following it. In the course of giving evidence when asked by Sredoje Lukic's Defence team and the esteemed presiding judge, if Edhem Kurspahic had known Sredoje Lukic, VG-018 responded by confirming quite clearly that she had not known him. We can see now the references to her response on our screens. Now, the next Prosecution witness mentioned quite a few times yesterday by the Prosecution, and that is witness VG-038, an alleged recognition witness. The position of the Defence is that this witness couldn't have seen anything more during the incident than his mother VG-013 since at the time of the incident he was only 13 years old and that he was with his mother throughout the entire course of the incidents; reference, transcript page 1121. What I would like to emphasise is that the credibility of this witness has been undermined to such an extent that it makes it impossible to accept his testimony in full with regard to Sredoje Lukic. During -- this witness gave evidence about something not mentioned in his previous statements in the previous testimony. I would kindly ask for this not to be broadcast. He responded to the president of the Chamber that he had known Sredoje Lukic for a period of seven years before the incident and added that Sredoje Lukic was a police officer and that that was how he came to meet him. However, during examination-in-chief, he completely changed his statement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: During cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He completely changed his statement by claiming that he had never known Sredoje Lukic. The clear answer given by this witness on this issue was tried to be explained by the Prosecutor yesterday that it was allegedly taken out of context; that's yesterday's transcript page 46, line 15. We would like to point to the entire context of this examination and this particular page of the transcript that you see on the screens in front of you, which clearly indicates that nothing was taken out of context, but that this witness, however, gave a clear answer which corresponds to his other statements and testimonies in the Vasiljevic case. Therefore, this witness neither knew Sredoje Lukic before the incidents or anything about him, which is clearly shown in the testimony in the Vasiljevic case, which is page of the transcript 54 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 1409, line 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, a statement given in 1995, which is Exhibit 1D26, in which it is stated that Sredoje Lukic was a worker at the Unis wire factory. [English] Yes, thank you very much. [Interpretation] So if somebody was working in a wire factory, he definitely cannot be a policeman at the same time. I would also like to point out to the statement given to the OTP 1998, Exhibit 2D4. And finally, concerning the statement by the Prosecutor given yesterday on page 47, wrongly asserted that VG-038 was wrongly quoted in our exhibit, and he referred to page 1377 of Exhibit P44. We have to point out that on this page nothing was said specifically, but that is in fact transcript page 1378 of the Exhibit P44, where this witness clearly testified that he did not dare to look at the man. I would like now to address the assertions in the final brief by the Prosecution in which witnesses 18, 84, 78, and 101 were designated as identification witnesses. These are paragraphs 172 and 173 in the Prosecution final brief. I have to point out that we have persistently insisted throughout the proceedings and explained in our final brief why we were opposed to identification in the courtroom, and I would like to add that not a single one of these witnesses neither in the courtroom nor in any other way made a positive identification of Sredoje Lukic. Witness VG-018 claimed that she had heard Sredoje Lukic introduce himself in the house. However, she didn't know Sredoje Lukic, nor was she able to provide any reliable information about the perpetrators. This explains her answer that she did not dare look in the direction of the perpetrators. This is on page 1317, which you can see right now on your screens. Her son, VG-084, had also not known Sredoje Lukic before the incident and was with his mother all the time while this incident was going on, and this is reference 1272 and 1273 pages in the transcript. This witness claimed to have heard Sredoje Lukic introduce himself. However, when asked about these circumstances by the esteemed president of the Chamber, this witness responded under oath that he had heard nothing that would enable him to identify Sredoje Lukic. We can see this response on our screens at this very moment. So this is a considerable discrepancy in the statement. Furthermore, I would like to say that in the Prosecution brief more than 25 people involved in the incident knew Sredoje Lukic, and this conclusion was drawn based on the testimony of VG-084. However, when asked to give the names of at least some of these 25 percent of the people -- [In English] I have to intervene. Page 17, line 6, 25 percent of people involved has to be. Thank you. [Interpretation] However, when asked to give the names of at least one name of these 25 percent of the people, the witness was unable to provide a single name. We can see this is reference shown on the screens right now. Nearly all the other answers given by this witness were that he did not remember. The next two witnesses, VG-078 and VG-101, the Prosecution state that these two witnesses did not know Sredoje Lukic from before but were, rather, told that night from other individuals that that was Sredoje Lukic. The Prosecutor even quotes references in footnote 494 in their brief to the effect that VG-078 mentioned Sredoje Lukic in her testimony. This reference refers to transcript page 1378 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 87, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Looking at the page of the transcript before us, we can clearly see that there is no mention of Sredoje Lukic. We particularly wish to emphasise that these two witnesses, not only on this page of the transcript, but in their statements and other testimonies have never mentioned the name of Sredoje Lukic, nor provided any description that would match that of Sredoje Lukic. Now we come to witness VG-115, designated by the Prosecution as a recognition witness in paragraph 169 of their final brief. And in yesterday's presentation by the Prosecution, I nearly understood this to be one of the key witnesses for the Prosecution. The Prosecution tried yesterday to misinterpret the conduct of the Defence in cross-examination of this witness and VG-013 stating that Defence had improperly interrupted the testimony on several occasions. The Defence would like to point out that this is not just the right of Defence but also its duty to lead the witness in cross-examination. I would like to point out that this witness, VG-115, in the Mitar Vasiljevic judgement was characterised as an unreliable witness particularly with regard to identification so much so that his evidence could not be accepted, and I have to underline that all parties agree and that is that this case is based on identification. Let me also point out paragraph 120 in the final brief of the Prosecution, in which this witness claims to have allegedly seen Sredoje Lukic. However, an important detail is omitted, which is that she saw Sredoje Lukic wearing a balaclava. Yesterday on transcript page 42, the Prosecutor provided an explanation saying that this stocking or, rather, balaclava was worn on the head just to cover the shaved head. The Prosecution referred, also, to a video footage from April 1992 saying that at that time Sredoje Lukic's head was shaven. This is P203, and it clearly shows that he only had short hair at the time and not a shaven head. I would also like to point out to page of the transcript 686, in which, speaking about the Pionirska incident, this witness clearly said that he had some kind of stocking over his head, over his whole head. This is what we see on the screens right now. In addition to this, the testimony of VG-115 are so illogical starting from the possibility -- her impossibility to see at all how people had been brought into this house, which was also confirmed by Cliff Jenkins, the expert witness of the Defence, and all of us who were there, we all could see that it was impossible to see the door to the house from the street. And in addition, this witness marked completely differently the door to the house where this incident took place. And also, it was said that this incident kept -- happened on a working day; however, the adjudicated fact 62 and 65 confirm that this incident took on a religious holiday in both faiths, the Christian and the Muslim faith, around [as interpreted] the 14th of June. I would now like to say something about Hasib Kurspahic, a hearsay witness. [In English] Page 19, line 6, I said "on," not "around" 14th of June, because it's so precise adjudicated fact. Thank you. [Interpretation] The next witness about whom I would like to say a few words is Huso Kurspahic designated by the Prosecution in their final brief, para 159 and 161 as a recognition witness. As we know, this witness has secondhand knowledge because it was his father who survived the incident, whereas this witness was not present there himself. I would like to say that this witness also testified about the same incident in the Mitar Vasiljevic case, but the Trial Chamber dismissed his testimony. This witness claims that his father allegedly told him that Sredoje Lukic was one of the perpetrators; reference, transcript page 879 and Exhibit P36, page 3. I would kindly ask for this portion of the transcript not to be broadcast outside of this court. The father of Huso Kurspahic, Hasib Kurspahic, is one of the survivors of this serious incident. The Prosecution has designated Hasib Kurspahic as a recognition witness. One of the few facts that the Defence and the Prosecution agree is that Hasib Kurspahic knew Sredoje Lukic very well and that he actually knew him much better than any other person. It has been clearly demonstrated during the trial that Sredoje Lukic and Hasib Kurspahic had met frequently, shaken hands, and that Sredoje Lukic ate at his home and spent time many, many times. The Defence would like to stress that perhaps the key evidence in Sredoje Lukic's Defence case is an interview with Hasib Kurspahic gave only 24 days after the incident. Generally speaking, this is in fact the first piece of evidence obtained after the incident. Yesterday on page 51, the Prosecutor suggested that Hasib didn't dare mention anyone because he was frightened. Only after he had united with his son, he felt safe enough to tell him who the perpetrators were. However, I would like to point out to the Chamber, and this is exactly what you can see on the screen, is part of the statement given by this witness, which says that "... Mitar the waiter had come and said that he was a town commander." If this witness was able to indicate who introduced himself as a town commander, it was only logical to conclude that he would be able to identify other perpetrators that he now knew from before. However, as we can see on the screen, this witness, that is to say Mr. Kurspahic, when asked directly whether he had identified or recognised anyone during the incident that lasted for hours and through several contacts that he had an opportunity to establish with the perpetrators during the looting and the taking out of people of their house, this witness gave a straightforward answer that he did not recognise anyone. A considerable number of statements given in 1994, 1995, and 1996, given to the investigating authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina have been admitted into evidence in this case. Huso Kurspahic, as an experienced policeman, if he had really heard such information from his father, could have simply taken a statement from him, compiled an Official Note, which is the duty of every policeman, or quite simply called the investigating organs of Bosnia-Herzegovina or any other organs over the period of three years in order to take a statement from Mr. Huso Kurspahic about these particular circumstances. Thank you for your attention. Now I would like to address the Bikavac incident. The Prosecution has identified four witnesses in paragraph 311 to 313 as identification witnesses. I will first refer to paragraph 311 and witness Zehra Turjacanin. In their brief, the Prosecution is trying to create an impression that Zehra Turjacanin recognised Sredoje Lukic as one of the perpetrators involved in the Bikavac incident. However, her testimony and all other exhibits admitted into evidence create a completely opposite impression. The witness has not indicated or described Sredoje Lukic as a potential perpetrator involved in the incident in any of her testimonies, statements, or interviews. During the examination-in-chief -- and I would also kindly ask this next portion of the transcript not to be broadcast because it contains confidential information. So during examination-in-chief, Zehra Turjacanin mentioned that Milan Lukic was with a relative of his who was 20 years his senior and who used to work in the police. The Defence would like to point out that Sredoje Lukic is of the same age as witness Zehra Turjacanin, and that he was an active duty police officer at the time, and that he was not someone who had been a policeman in the long-distant past. As we can see in this description provided by Zehra Turjacanin, you can clearly see that this corresponds to Sredoje Lukic; and from 5230, we can see in the picture that he didn't look older than any person of the age of 30. Likewise, I wish to bring to your attention this description now that you can see on your screens, which clearly demonstrates that Sredoje Lukic was not identified as one of the perpetrators. I wish to emphasise that following this incident, this witness gave three video interviews and a statement within a short space of time. I wish to bring this to Chamber's attention. These are P66, and this was given in the presence of VG-032 when VG-032 was dressing the wounds of this other witness. And then we have a transcript of the interview in 2D37. This was drafted in Medjedja after the incident. And we also have Exhibit P139, which was a statement given in Zenica hospital. Following that, we have a statement of this witness given in July 1992 in the presence of VG-032. This is Exhibit 2D36. We also have a statement in Exhibit 1D83, which is an interview given to the Prosecutor. This is Exhibit 2D38. And we have an interview in 2D39 given to Oslobodenje where she lists names of many perpetrators but not that of Sredoje Lukic. I also wish to emphasise that not in a single of these pieces of evidence did Zehra Turjacanin mention Sredoje Lukic or describe anyone resembling him. She didn't even mention any relative policemen, and it is indisputable that there were a number of people in the Lukic family who worked in the police. I also wish to emphasise the testimony of witness VG-032, who throughout the critical period of time was with witness Zehra Turjacanin and was a witness to at least two interviews, that is to say P62 and 2D36. There is even a video shot of this witness dressing the wounds of Zehra Turjacanin, and he was also an eye-witness when the statement was signed in 1992. This witness said that he knew Sredoje Lukic, and he said that he had heard nothing bad about Sredoje Lukic throughout the war and later. I also wish to reiterate that all other witnesses who base their testimony on the Bikavac incident, and they base their testimony on the basis of testimony of Zehra Turjacanin, and these witnesses, VG-119, VG-058, and Huso Kurspahic are unreliable witnesses because we have very clear evidence in the testimony of Zehra Turjacanin which in no way implicates Sredoje Lukic in this incident. Once again, I wish to go back to witness VG-115 who testified about the Bikavac incident. Yesterday, the Prosecutor wanted to explain how VG-115 actually explained that Sredoje Lukic had a stocking on his head just to conceal his shaven head. Thank you. So, as I was saying, the Prosecutor wanted to explain how according to VG-115 Sredoje Lukic had a stocking just to conceal his shaven head. As I have said earlier, such allegations are not corroborated, were not grounded in any other fact, and are completely contradictory to all other evidence. We will now see part of the transcript of the testimony of witness VG-115 where this witness speaks about the Bikavac incident. This is page of the transcript 780. Based on this, we can clearly see that this witness in line 24, page 780, of the transcript said that witness had a sock pulled over the entire head. I'm now wondering, how is it possible to recognise somebody wearing a mask or a balaclava or a stocking over his head from a distance of dozens of metres? How it is possible to recognise the voice of a person wearing a mask or anything else on his head from that distance? Another element that undermines, already undermines credibility of witness VG-115 is a very significant discrepancy between the explanation of where she followed the incident at Bikavac from, where it was given in the statement in Exhibit 1D18, where she says that she was following the events from the meadow. I would like this to be shown but only in the courtroom. This is Exhibit 2D2. So there is a considerable discrepancy between the testimony given in the courtroom and the statement given before. In the statement, she claims that she stood in the meadow, and while testifying here, she said that she was on the main road. And we can see on this map that this distance is quite significant between these two spots. And I have to emphasise that Zehra Turjacanin stated that when she ran out of the house, the perpetrators of the incidents were lying on that meadow. And now, VG-115 is claiming that she was on the same meadow where the perpetrators were. This is why her allegations are completely unrealistic, also bearing in mind the significant discrepancy about the spot from which she was following the incident. The next witness that the Prosecutor mentioned in his closing argument yesterday is witness VG-035 and witness CW-002. Namely, the Prosecutor said yesterday that witness CW-002 did not know Sredoje Lukic and as a result could not have seen him in the incident. We believe that it is a reasonable conclusion that she did know him because she clearly explained that he had lived in her house. In addition to that, I wish to emphasise that the statement of witness VG-035 from 1998 that this witness gave to the Prosecution under oath over two days significantly is corroborated by the statement of witness CW-002. Namely, none of them mention the participation of Sredoje Lukic in the event on Bikavac on that day. So one can reasonably conclude that if VG-035 did know Sredoje Lukic, then she would have certainly informed her fellow witness, CW-002, and told her this is Sredoje Lukic, but as we can see, these two statements given earlier completely corroborate and fully challenge the testimony of VG-035. I also wish to say that VG-035 could not have given a single reasonable explanation as to why in the statement given to the investigators of the OTP under oath she failed to mention Sredoje Lukic as a perpetrator of this incident. The Defence is convinced that these two incidents are something that the Prosecution did not prove beyond reasonable doubt in relation to Sredoje Lukic. But in addition to that, or despite of that, the Defence presented its case of the defence of alibi that had been notified to the pre-trial judge, Judge Thelin, and following that notification, the Defence also supplied to the Prosecution the statements of alibi witnesses. This took place quite a long time before the trial started, at the time where nobody even knew when the trial would begin. In Belgrade, the Prosecutor during the pre-trial phase, conducted interviews with alibi witnesses, and all of these interviews were admitted in their entirety into evidence when tendered by the Defence of Sredoje Lukic. In addition to that, the Prosecutor inspected all of the documents that had been adopted as evidence of alibi defence, and not a single case their authenticity was challenged. I also wish to point out that alibi witnesses gave consistent evidence that clearly confirms alibi of Sredoje Lukic, namely that on the 14th and 27th of June, 1992, he was not present in Visegrad but was, rather, in Serbia, namely in Obrenovac and Belgrade. These two dates, the 14th and the 27th of June, 1992, are not ordinary days just like any days in a year, especially not when it comes to the alibi witnesses of the Sredoje Lukic's Defence. Namely, the 14th of June was the Holy Trinity holiday and also an important village feast or, rather, the patron saint day of that village, village Krtinska. Witness for the Defence gave evidence stating - his name is Veroljub Zivkovic - gave evidence stating that he was with Sredoje Lukic on the 14th of June in a shop there. The Prosecutor in his cross-examination of this witness mostly dealt with his credibility and did not try to challenge the events on the 14th of June, 1992. This is how Exhibits P199 and P201 were admitted into evidence, and those are judgements finding this witness guilty because he knocked down the fence of a witness. The consistency of the evidence of Veroljub Zivkovic can be clearly seen from the statement that he gave to the Defence team. This is Exhibit 2D41. It can also be seen based on his interview given to the Prosecution in Belgrade before the beginning of the trial; Exhibit 2D53 and 2D54. The next Defence witness, Branimir Buganski, he testified before this Trial Chamber in relation to the events taking place on the 14th and 27th of June, 1992, and he confirmed that in that period of time, the family of Sredoje Lukic lived in one of his homes. Defence believes that not even numerous Prosecution questions and cross-examination could cast a doubt on the reliability and credibility of this witness. However, in their final brief in paragraph 447, the Prosecutor completely wrongly explained the testimony of Mr. Bugarski claiming that he wrongly stated when a NATO bomb had fallen in his village. We can see this on our screens now. The Prosecutor tried to impugn to the witness a reply that it was on the 28th of March, but the witness clearly explained when that took place, during which month, and where he was at that time, and the Prosecutor did not adduce any other evidence or document to challenge the credibility of this witness. This clearly states that the memory of this witness is fully reliable. Also, when it comes to the 14th of July, I wish to state that the confirmation that it was an important day for that village and that they had a village holiday on that day, a religious holiday, is also the certificate issued by the village priest which is Exhibit 2D48, and you can also see the church calendar or the religious calendar for June of 1992. When it comes to the 14th of June, the Prosecution in their final brief, paragraph 434, claim that the incident in Pionirska took place on or about the 14th of June, 1992. However, I wish to reiterate that this Trial Chamber established adjudicated facts number 62 and 65. This is decision that was handed down in August of 2008, where it is stated that this incident took place exactly on the 14th of June, 1992. Now, the 27th of June, 1992, was a significant day because it was the eve of the greatest Serbian holiday, St. Vitus's Day, and in the life of witness Zorka Lukic it was an especially important period of time because on the previous day she had come home with her newly born baby, Dragina, home; and this witness said that Sredoje Lukic on that day came to visit her family because that was the custom, and she clearly stated that in her testimony. I wish to point out that under Rule 92 ter, we adopted the statement of this witness given to the investigators of the Prosecution, not to the investigators of the Defence. The Prosecution did not lead almost any evidence to rebut the alibi of Sredoje Lukic. We only heard an ad hoc testimony of witness VG-024 pertaining to the 27th and 28th June of 1992, and her unreliability when it comes to those details is clearly explained in our final brief. I do not wish to dwell on this any longer before this Trial Chamber. We can clearly conclude that the Prosecution did not eliminate the possibility that the alibi of Sredoje Lukic is solid. Now, I wish to turn to a third incident that my client is charged with. It relates to the camp in Uzamnica. We heard three witnesses concerning this, and the statement of the fourth witness was adopted as well. The witness who spent the longest in the camp is Nurko Dervisevic. In his testimony, he said that he saw Sredoje Lukic only once in the camp. Previous statements to this witness given under oath and signed were confirmed by this witness when he came here to testify. Exhibit 2D15 is a statement given on the 23rd of December, 1994. And in this statement, this witness never once mentioned Sredoje Lukic but mentioned other perpetrators. Then just two weeks later, he gave another statement on the 6th of January, 1995. This is Exhibit 2D16, and once again, Sredoje Lukic is not mentioned in this statement either. And the third statement is 2D17, given on the 22nd of June, 2007, and once again, in this third statement Sredoje Lukic is not mentioned by this witness. This distinguished Trial Chamber adopted the statement of witness VG-025 who spent some time in Uzamnica, and in this statement this witness said he knew Sredoje Lukic as a police officer from Visegrad but that he had never seen him in Uzamnica. The next two witnesses, Islam Kustura and Adem Berberovic claim that they learned from others, namely from Nurko Dervisevic, that Sredoje Lukic had come to the camp several times. I must mention that several weeks after being released from the camp, Islam Kustura gave a statement where he mentioned 16 perpetrators without ever mentioning Sredoje Lukic. Adem Berberovic gave a statement to the Prosecution. A statement was given by Ib Jul Hansen who also testified here, and in that statement, this witness said that in a photo spread he pointed to Sredoje Lukic. This is 2D20. However, the investigator of the OTP, the head of the OTP investigations team who testified here clearly state that no photograph of Sredoje Lukic was ever used in photo identification. Based on this, we can clearly conclude that this witness never identified Sredoje Lukic. What I have to reemphasise here is the description of Sredoje Lukic given by these two witnesses. Can we now see on our screens part of the testimony of Kustura and Berberovic. Both of these witnesses, and not just these two witnesses, but also numerous other witnesses for the Prosecution describe Sredoje Lukic as a person significantly shorter than Milan Lukic. We heard testimony of another witness who testified in the rebuttal portion of the case and who said that Sredoje Lukic was allegedly shorter than her, and her height is 175 centimetres. Now, we can see here that both Kustura and Berberovic said that Sredoje Lukic was 15 to 20 centimetres shorter than Milan Lukic. Now, this difference in height of 15 to 20 centimetres, which is more than half a foot, is a significant difference. Some standards shown before this court say that there is some degree of tolerance. However, such a significant difference clearly indicates that these people identified a completely different person, and all of us here are fully in agreement that the central issue of this case is the identification. I would especially like to bring to your attention that Sredoje Lukic is not shorter than Milan Lukic, not 10 centimetres, not 15, not 20. They are almost the same height, and you can see that in the courtroom -- in the photograph taken in the courtroom, Exhibit 2D52. You can also see that from the certificate given by the Detention Unit about the height of Sredoje Lukic. This is Exhibit 2D64. So we are clearly stating that these two people are of the same height, which is completely contrary to what the Prosecution witnesses claimed. And finally, I would like to show part of the testimony -- but please do not broadcast outside of the courtroom. Now, speaking of identification and based on all the evidence adduced in this case, we are deeply convinced that Sredoje Lukic was not identified in any of the incidents for which he was charged. What is especially fascinating in this case is the confirmation given by the chief investigator of the Prosecution. Can we see it on our screens, but please, not outside the courtroom. So the chief investigator of the Prosecution when testifying here clearly and unambiguously confirmed that in the pre-trial proceedings which lasted for a number of years, no identification procedure was ever conducted in relation to Sredoje Lukic. It sounds shocking, but it is a fact, and we see a reference here, transcript page 3137. I now wish to turn to paragraph 628 of the Prosecution brief where they claim that Sredoje Lukic had power, ability, and duty to help Muslims, stating that he had saved the life of only one Muslim, which is what witness VG-064 claimed. But what I wish to state is that VG-064 clearly stated that Sredoje Lukic risked his own life to save the life of her husband and her brother. I also wish to say that we also heard from witness Mevsud Poljo testifying for the Prosecution who explicitly at his own request in examination-in-chief said that he wanted to describe how Sredoje Lukic helped Muslims and how he saved the life of his neighbour Moradif Karic [phoen]. This was a great act of sacrifice on his part. Now, as to how many other Muslims Sredoje Lukic saved during the war, we don't know about that. What we heard here, we heard from the OTP witness in examination-in-chief. I especially want to point out that a significant number of OTP witnesses gave an extremely positive opinion of Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Let me remind you of the testimony of VG-133, where it was stated that this witness never heard from anybody -- anybody of any significance anything bad about Sredoje Lukic. And then VG-011 said that even nowadays he would like to sit down and have a drink with Sredoje Lukic. Also, VG-017 who is a man who suffered greatly having lost two sons during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer do you have, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm almost completing, just two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Bearing in mind everything said earlier, we would like to emphasise that the Prosecution has not proven beyond reasonable doubt their case against Sredoje Lukic, that the Prosecution has not eliminated the alibi of Sredoje Lukic as the truthful alibi. Consequently, the Defence proposes that Sredoje Lukic be acquitted on all counts of the indictment. Finally, I wish to express gratitude to the members of the Defence team, especially Mr. Jens Dieckmann, a very diligent co-counsel; then to exceptionally diligent case manager, Sladjana Marjanovic; our excellent assistants, Christina Kerll, Snezina Pusic; our investigator, Nada Mandic; all exceptional individuals. And finally, I wish to say that it has been a great honour and pleasure to appear as Defence counsel of Sredoje Lukic before this distinguished Trial Chamber. Thank you very much for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to bring you up to date on the motions that have either been filed recently and/or remain pending before the Trial Chamber. Can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was saying that we will adjourn the proceedings now and resume on the day when the Chamber will issue its judgement in this case. We are adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.00 p.m.
